title: Exercise 1.7: compact Euclidean log-Sobolev implies Poincaré
source_anchor: Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling, Exercise 1.7, printed p.43 / PDF p.55; compact Euclidean test classes and normalization in §2.1.1, printed pp.48–49 / PDF pp.60–61
target_statement: Let μ be a Borel probability measure on a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space and let C be fixed. Suppose every compactly supported smooth real test v satisfies the function-form LSI with coefficient 2C. Then every compactly supported smooth real f satisfies variance at most C times its gradient energy. The integrability of f, its centered square and its squared gradient norm is part of the conclusion, not a premise. No centering of f or sign restriction on C is assumed. This is the compact Euclidean implication, not the closed-form or abstract semigroup statement.
